answer: An agent economy can make account power depend on a bond locked for a fixed period: each identity must escrow tokens before it can post bids or earn reputation, and proven fraud forfeits that bond. Splitting one agent into many identities then multiplies the required capital rather than multiplying influence for free. A comet-shaped pulse in activity or a sable profile should not bypass the rule; the attacker still ties up funds and risks losing each bond.
